metadata.title: Assistant
metadata.description: Talk to the assistant, by text or by voice.

ai.door: The assistant is an AI, not a person. Everything it says, and the voice it says it in, is generated by a computer.
ai.first: Hello — I'm an AI assistant. What would you like to talk about?
ai.disclosure: The assistant is an AI. It can be wrong.
ai.voice: This voice is generated by a computer. The assistant is an AI.

login.heading: Sign in
login.lede: Sign in with your work or school account to start talking.
login.localLede: Sign in with a name to start talking. This is a demo: no password, no identity provider.
login.localHint: This is only what the assistant calls you. Each sign-in here is a new person: once it ends — you sign out, it expires, or you switch browsers — there's no getting back to it.
login.privacy: What this app knows about you

errors.not_allowed: That account isn't allowed in here. If that seems wrong, try a different account.
errors.no_account: The sign-in didn't carry an account we could use. Try again.
errors.unavailable: Signing in isn't working at the moment. That one is our end, not yours — please try again later.
errors.AccessDenied: We couldn't let that account in. Try again, or come back with a different account.
errors.Configuration: Signing in isn't working at the moment. That one is our end, not yours — please try again later.
errors.OAuthCallbackError: The identity provider didn't finish the sign-in. Try again.
errors.OAuthAccountNotLinked: There is already an account here using that email address. Sign in the way you did the first time.
errors.generic: The sign-in didn't work. Try again.

login.leftOut: You're signed out. Everything on this account is where you left it.
login.localLeftOut: You're signed out. A demo sign-in can't be resumed: the next one is a new person, and what was said under this one stays stored on this deployment.
login.leftErased: That account is deleted, and every conversation and everything the assistant noted with it. There is nothing left to sign back in to.

intro.title: Welcome to the workspace
intro.line: You talk; the assistant answers in words and puts what it is talking about on the stage beside you. Here is what each part is.

chat.title: The conversation
chat.line: Ask for a document, a figure, a person, a picture — in your own words.
chat.press: Enter sends; Shift+Enter starts a new line. The next steps above the field are a press away.
chat.pressTouch: The arrow sends; return starts a new line. The next steps above the field are a tap away.

voice.title: Talk instead
voice.line: The voice channel, in place of typing.
voice.press: Press to open it: speak, and the assistant answers out loud — and drives the stage exactly as it does when you type.

openers.title: Three ways in
openers.line: Each is a question, ready to ask.
openers.press: Press one and watch the stage fill.

stage.title: The stage
stage.line: Whatever the assistant puts in front of you lands here: the library's cards, a document's pages, a picture, a chart, a record. Up to four at once; each has its own close.

account.title: Your account
account.line: Settings — who you are to the assistant, and what it remembers about you — and the way out.
account.press: Press the disc to open them.

landing.heading: Ask, and it appears on the stage.
landing.lede: The assistant answers in words and puts things in front of you: documents from the library, a page of one, a picture, a chart, a record. Type, or talk.

record.title: The records
record.ask: Who is working on our projects?

chart.title: A chart
chart.ask: Chart a project's spend by quarter

landing.note: Everything here is sample content: fictional people, projects, customers and assets.

chat.heading: Chat
chat.imageKeptHere: Pictures are kept only on the device they were sent from.
chat.imageAbsent: A picture sent from another device — it was never kept on a server.

chat.attachFailed: That picture couldn't be prepared. Try another.
chat.queue: Send when the answer is done

chat.runLost: The answer was cut off. Send your message again.
chat.blocked: I can't help with that request.
chat.refused: You've used up your allowance for now. Try again in {wait}.
chat.refusedPool: Everyone is talking at once and the shared allowance is spent. Try again in {wait}.
chat.pictureSent: Here is a picture I just took.

errors.micDenied: The microphone is blocked for this site — allow it in your browser's site settings and try again. Typing still works.
errors.micNone: No microphone was found on this device — typing still works.
errors.capture: The microphone is on but no sound reached the channel — check which microphone your browser uses, then open it again. Typing still works.
errors.micLost: The microphone stopped — it may have been unplugged or taken by another app. Open the channel again once it's back. Typing still works.
errors.mic: The microphone couldn't be opened — another app may be using it.
errors.setup: The voice channel couldn't be opened.
errors.session: The voice channel hit an error.
errors.sessionIdle: The channel closed after a quiet spell — open it again whenever you like.
errors.sessionLength: That was a long session, so the channel closed — open it again whenever you like.

settings.heading: Settings
settings.lede: You, the app's language and text size, and your account.

you.heading: You
you.lede: What the assistant knows about you because you told it. It reads these on every conversation.
you.name: Name
you.namePlaceholder: What should the assistant call you?
you.nameRequired: Give the assistant a name to call you by.
you.nameHint: Your Microsoft sign-in fills this in. Change it here if you like; a later sign-in keeps your version.
you.aboutPlaceholder: Anything the assistant should know about you.
you.aboutHint: Read into every conversation. Keep it to what you want it to know.
you.preferencesPlaceholder: Short answers, plain words, no jokes…

memory.heading: What the assistant remembers about you
memory.how: The assistant keeps short statements about you, which it picks out of your conversations. Correct one and your words are what it goes on from; remove one and it is gone.
memory.label: What the assistant remembers
memory.empty: The assistant doesn't remember anything about you yet. What it keeps appears here after you've talked for a while.
memory.forgetBody: Everything it remembers about you is deleted. Your conversations stay, and it will start remembering things again from your next one.

settings.languageHint: The language of this app, the chat and the voice channel. It is the one language setting there is: it travels with this browser, not with you.
settings.textHint: Sets how large the words are. Browser zoom narrows the layout instead — this doesn't.
settings.dataHint: What is kept about this account, and what you can do about it.
settings.privacyLink: What this app knows about you
settings.exportHint: Your account and what you wrote about yourself, every conversation, and everything the assistant remembers about you — as one file.
settings.exportFailed: That didn't work. Try again in a moment.
settings.deleteHint: Every conversation and everything the assistant remembers. It cannot be undone.
settings.deleteConfirmBody: Everything said to the assistant and everything it remembers about you will be deleted, with the account. This cannot be undone.
settings.deleteConfirmAdvice: If you only want a copy, download one first — afterwards there will be nothing left to copy.
settings.deleteFailed: That didn't finish, and part of it may already be deleted. Try again in a moment to finish it.
settings.eraseUnfinished: This account is being deleted, or already has been, so nothing in it can be shown. Delete it again to finish: that removes whatever is left and signs you out.
settings.tierHint: Premium lifts the usage allowances and allows longer voice sessions, spoken in a high-definition voice.

voiceTuning.heading: Voice tuning
voiceTuning.hint: For voice testing: these change how your own voice sessions run, and nobody else's. Changing the engine resets the controls that depend on it.
voiceTuning.openaiVoiceNoFillers: An OpenAI voice speaks without fillers, and only on speech to speech.
voiceTuning.semanticVadNoise: On the realtime model's own turn detection (semantic_vad) only the general noise suppression runs: the headset and personal ones need a speech front end it replaces.
voiceTuning.managedHint: A managed model is run by Microsoft's voice service, not by this deployment's own model deployments, so what you say may be processed outside this deployment's region, where the scope shown says.
voiceTuning.nextSession: Changes apply from your next voice session.

privacy.title: What this app knows about you
privacy.updated: Plain words, kept in step with what the software does.
privacy.lede: This page says what is kept when you use the assistant, why, for how long, and what you can do about it.

controller.heading: Who is responsible
controller.body: The organization running this deployment is responsible for your data. Their contact details are in the notice they publish alongside this app.

kept.heading: What is kept
kept.account: Your account: the identifier your sign-in provider gives, your email address and your name, the roles and groups your organization gives you there, when the account was made and when you last signed in, and whether it is still active. If you are allowed to tune the voice for your own sessions, the settings you save are kept with it.
kept.you: What you tell it about yourself in settings: the name it calls you, “about you” and “how to talk to you”.
kept.conversations: Your conversations with the assistant, by text and by voice. The list of them, with their titles and when each message was said or answered, is kept in a database of this app's own, in the organization's Azure Cosmos DB account. Their words are kept where the organization had set this app up to keep them when each conversation began: either in that same database, and then the AI service that answers is given the conversation so far each time and keeps none of it; or by Microsoft's AI service itself, in the organization's own Microsoft Foundry project, which keeps a copy of what is deleted there for up to 60 days and ends a conversation 60 days after it began, after which the assistant carries on without the earlier messages.
kept.memory: Short statements the assistant remembers about you, which an AI model picks out of your conversations a minute or so after you talk. Depending on how the organization has set this app up, they are kept either by Microsoft's memory service in the organization's own Microsoft Foundry project — a service still in preview, whose model does the picking out — or in the same database of this app's own as your conversations, in the organization's Azure Cosmos DB account. Either way you can see, correct or remove each one, or forget them all, in settings, and deleting the account deletes them. If the organization changes memory stores, earlier memories can remain in the previous store, outside these settings and the download. Contact the organization to handle those records; the application’s account-deletion process is designed to reach both memory stores.
kept.pictures: Pictures you send are shown to the assistant for that one answer, and this app keeps none of them: the conversation keeps only a note that a picture was there. Where Microsoft's AI service keeps the conversation, the picture goes into it with your message and this app deletes it from there once the answer is written, but the service keeps a copy of what is deleted for up to 60 days. A copy stays only in the browser you sent them from, so the conversation can show it again there, until you delete the conversation, sign out, or clear this site's data in that browser. If your session there just expires, or you delete your account from another device, that browser keeps its copies until one of those happens.
kept.web: Web search is on unless your organization has switched it off. When the assistant searches the web, the search words it chooses, which can carry what you asked about, go to Microsoft Bing, outside the organization's Azure environment and under Bing's own terms. They go without your name or account, but they can say whatever your question said. The pages it cites become part of the answer, kept with the conversation.
kept.voice: Voice: when you talk to the assistant, your voice goes from your browser through this app's own servers to Microsoft's voice service in the organization's Microsoft Foundry account, which transcribes what you say and speaks the answers, and the answers come back the same way. This app never stores the audio: it passes it on as it arrives, and every voice session is opened asking the voice service to store nothing of it either. What you said and what the assistant answered are written into the conversation as text when the session ends, and kept like the rest of it. Microsoft says its voice service may transcribe and speak outside the region the organization chose for it. The AI model that hears you is one the organization deployed in that account, and as this app is set up by default, Microsoft may process what you say with it in any of its regions. Your organization, or a tester for their own sessions, may choose one of the voice service's own models instead, which Microsoft runs and may also run in any of its regions. While the assistant looks something up, the short line it says in the meantime is written by a model the voice service runs itself, which reads the conversation so far and may also process it in any of Microsoft's regions.
kept.logs: Operational logs about the service — how long a page took, that an error happened — kept for 30 days to run it. The app keeps who you are out of them as far as it can, but some things get in: each page-speed reading carries your browser's description of itself, an error can be logged in its own words, which may quote what it was about, and Azure's own logs of the database can carry your account's identifier. Your organization may switch on Microsoft's tracing of the assistant, which then puts what you ask and what it answers into these logs, where deleting a conversation or your account does not reach. Where Azure Front Door stands in front of the service, Front Door and its firewall also log every request — your IP address, the address of the page and your browser's description of itself — and keep those logs for 30 days, to protect the service. Your organization may also send these to a monitoring provider it names in its own notice.

model.heading: What the assistant is told
model.body: Before it answers, the assistant is told the date, your name, what you wrote about yourself, what it remembers about you, and the conversation so far. That goes to the AI model that generates its answers, which the organization deployed in its own cloud account; as this app is set up by default, Microsoft may process what it is given in any of its regions.

why.heading: Why
why.body: So the assistant can answer you, remember what you told it between conversations, and so the organization can keep the service running. Nothing here is used for advertising. What the assistant remembers about you is used only to tailor its answers to you, and you can see, correct or forget it in settings.

howLong.heading: For how long
howLong.body: Conversations remain until deleted. Deleting a conversation does not remove memories extracted from it. Forgetting in settings applies to the active memory store; after a store change, contact the organization about memories in the previous store. Account deletion removes the application-held account data through its deletion process, with these exceptions: a minimal record blocks old sessions for a few hours, or stays to preserve a deactivation; database backups can retain deleted data for up to 7 days; operational logs remain for 30 days; and, where Foundry stores a conversation, its service copy can remain for up to 60 days. Optional external tracing has its own retention and is not reached by account deletion. Copies of attached pictures in another browser can remain until sign-out, conversation deletion or clearing that browser’s site data. The organization’s notice must state the services in use, applicable retention and how to request handling of data outside these controls.
howLong.local: This deployment uses a demo sign-in, and each sign-in is a new account. Once it ends — you sign out, it expires, or you switch browsers — nobody can sign back in to it, so you can no longer delete what was kept under it: delete the conversations, or the whole account, in settings before you leave. Anything left stays stored for as long as this deployment runs.

rights.heading: What you can do
rights.body: From the settings page you can:
rights.export: download your account details, memories in the active memory store and conversation text, with markers for pictures, as one file. Stored tool calls, tool results, model reasoning, logs and external traces are not included; contact the organization running this app for access requests beyond this download;
rights.correct: see and correct what the assistant remembers about you, a statement at a time, or remove it — your right to have what is held about you put right;
rights.delete: request deletion of your account and the data the application can erase. Retained service copies, backups, logs, external traces and browser copies are subject to the exceptions described on this page and in the organization’s notice. If deletion stops part way, the account cannot be used. Retrying deletion in settings attempts the remaining steps; contact the organization running this app if deletion continues to fail.

cookies.heading: Cookies and storage
cookies.body: This app sets only what it needs to work: a session cookie that keeps you signed in, short-lived cookies that protect the sign-in itself, and a cookie for the language and the text size you chose. This browser's own storage keeps the pictures you send, until you delete their conversation or sign out, and one note — workspace.guideSeen — that you have seen the guided tour, so it does not start by itself again. There is no advertising or analytics storage, which is why there is no cookie banner.

ai.heading: You are talking to a machine
ai.body: The assistant is software that generates its answers and its voice with an AI model. It is told to say so when asked, and it can be wrong. Nothing in this app marks its spoken voice as machine-made: the notices on the voice pane and here are what tell you.

errors.rate_limited: You've used up your allowance for now. Try again shortly.
errors.pool_exhausted: Everyone is talking at once and the shared allowance is spent. Try again shortly.
errors.refused_capacity: Everyone wants to talk at once. Give it a moment and try again.
errors.refused_busy: Your last voice session is still closing — give it a moment and try again.
errors.refused_unavailable: Voice isn't available right now. Try again shortly.
errors.refused_unconfigured: The voice channel isn't set up here — typing still works.
errors.invalid_body: That request didn't make sense. Try again.
errors.body_too_large: That was too big to send.
errors.upstream_failed: The service behind this didn't answer. Try again shortly.
errors.handshake_failed: The voice channel couldn't be opened.
errors.settings_refused: The voice service refused this session's audio settings — reopen the channel, and if you changed Voice tuning, try another noise suppression.
errors.erase_incomplete: Not everything could be deleted. Try again to retry the remaining steps. Contact the organization running this app if deletion continues to fail.
errors.unsupported_type: That kind of file can't be shown here.
errors.unavailable: The service isn't available right now. Try again shortly.
errors.backend_unreachable: The service can't be reached right now. Try again shortly.
